scientific_status: evidence-informed stylized conifer architectural concept; not an identified extinct species
artistic_choices: Seven-meter scale, crown spacing, small asymmetry and color are original design choices.

Each spray uses four pairs of bowed linear needle groups, with nearly parallel sides over the first 60 percent, narrow short terminal edges and independently pitched ranks. The modern Metasequoia reference supports curved linear needles, not r15 diamond leaves. Group size, count and fan area are artistic abstractions, not a fossil reconstruction.
Tubular bough bases flare into and are buried within the parent trunk; intentional closed-component intersections.
provenance: Original procedural geometry. References consulted only; no external mesh or image incorporated.
source_vertex_count_convention: Sum of authored mesh vertices across unique included meshes, before modifiers; no instances or modifiers.
topology_notes: Foliage uses closed eight-vertex curved linear groups with paired spread, width-to-length 0.27 and physical section thickness-to-width 0.07; foliage shares smooth normals and wood retains deliberate flat normals. All elements closed and opaque. Deliberate buried intersections at organic branch joins. No thick round foliage tubes or radial starburst clumps. Woody geometry and branchlet placements are inherited unchanged from r12. Two green palette groups follow older and younger shoot zones.

description.en: An original seven-meter conifer concept with open crown gaps, curved tapering boughs, four pairs of bowed linear groups with stable-width shoulders, short narrow tips and noncoplanar local pitch.
